the matrix elements of Thiemann’s Hamiltonian operator in the spin network basis have been calculated in closed form for all its natural orders and all trivalent spin networks.

the Euclidean Hamiltonian constraint operator, when acting on trivalent states in the spin-network Hilbert space, has matrix elements which are polynomials of degree 2 in the spin variables.

Thiemann's Euclidean Hamiltonian constraint operator, when acting on a trivalent graph, produces a linear combination of the following terms: a) a trivalent graph; b) two graphs, one with one more edge and the other one less; c) a graph with one more vertex; d) a graph with two more edges; e) a graph with a vertex of valence four and a graph with one less vertex.
